chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Mahbub from 'Isa ibn Sabih said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the thief who digs, the thief who climbs, and the thief who steals secretly, so he said: The thief who digs and the thief who climb are cut (hand), but the thief who steals secretly is not cut.

key_terms.الطَّرَّار: Thief who digs (into walls or ground to steal)
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: He is cut (referring to the hand)

ai.seo_question: Which types of thieves are subject to hand-cutting according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Ishtibār clarifies the application of *qat'* (hand amputation) by distinguishing between thieves who breach security through force or entry (digging/climbing) and those who steal discreetly. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction highlights that the severity of the punishment is tied to the method of intrusion and the violation of public security, rather than merely the act of taking property. It reflects the Imams' nuanced approach to *hudud*, ensuring that the harsh penalty is reserved for specific categories of theft that disrupt social order.
